title: Atomic last-owner guard — fixes concurrent-deactivation 0-owner self-lockout race
root_cause: In PATCH /api/users/:employee_id (src/http/user-mgmt.ts), the last-owner guard-read ("is there ANOTHER active tenant-owner?") ran in its OWN withTenantTx (READ COMMITTED, no FOR UPDATE), then a KC setUserEnabled(false)+revokeUserSessions happened, then the deactivating write ran in a SEPARATE withTenantTx. Two concurrent PATCH{active:false} on two DIFFERENT owners each passed the early guard (each saw the other still active, since neither write had landed), then both UPDATEd employee.deactivated_at — the write's WHERE only re-checked `deactivated_at IS NULL` for the SAME row, never the ≥1-owner invariant — leaving the tenant with ZERO active owners (self-lockout). Found in T-0658 round-3 final verification (spec §3.6).
fix_justification: Locking preferred over a partial constraint/trigger: (1) the guard already lives in a withTenantTx I could extend, so folding the authoritative guard into the SAME tx as the write is surgical and needs NO migration; (2) a partial UNIQUE index cannot express a per-group 'at least one' aggregate invariant; (3) a trigger enforcing '≥1 active owner' would STILL need its own SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (or SERIALIZABLE) to be race-safe under READ COMMITTED — two concurrent triggers counting owners each exclude their own target and both see ≥1, exactly the same race — so a trigger is not inherently stronger for THIS race, only broader in path coverage (out of T-0664 scope). The surgical lock at the one write path that mutates owner activity is the right scope.
fix_detail: On the deactivation path, INSIDE the write tx and BEFORE the UPDATE: `SELECT e.id ... JOIN role_assignment ra JOIN role r WHERE r.slug='tenant-owner' AND ra.confirmed_by IS NOT NULL AND window AND e.deactivated_at IS NULL ORDER BY e.id FOR UPDATE OF e` locks every active tenant-owner employee row (ORDER BY e.id → deterministic lock order → no deadlock). Then re-run the last-owner check (target still owner? any OTHER active owner?) under the lock. Concurrent owner-deactivations contend on the shared owner set and serialize: the second blocks until the first commits, re-reads (the just-deactivated owner drops out of the deactivated_at IS NULL set via READ COMMITTED EPQ), sees the target is now the last owner, and returns a sentinel → 409 LAST_OWNER without writing. The KC-first optimistic flip (setUserEnabled(false)) that already happened for the refused request is COMPENSATED by re-enabling the KC login, so a refused deactivation leaves no KC-disabled last owner. The pre-existing EARLY guard (before the KC flip) is retained as a fast-fail, preserving the sole-owner→KC-untouched and KC-unreachable→503-DB-untouched contracts.
mutation_proof: New db test 'T-0664: two concurrent deactivations of two different owners never leave 0 active owners' (ci/checks/db/user-mgmt.db.test.ts) uses a BarrierKcPort that rendezvous both requests at setUserEnabled (which sits AFTER the early guard, BEFORE the write), forcing the worst-case interleave deterministically every run: both clear the early guard before either writes. Asserts sorted statuses == [200,409], the 409 carries LAST_OWNER, exactly 1 active owner remains, and a compensating KC re-enable (setUserEnabled(...,true)) fired. RED with the FOR UPDATE neutralized (`if (false && active===false)`): both requests returned 200 → tenant would have 0 owners → test failed with 'expected [200,409], got [200,200]' (real PG :55432, ran in ~1.5s, no flakiness). GREEN with the fix restored (447-1409ms).
db_tests: ci/checks/db/user-mgmt.db.test.ts :: T-0664: two concurrent deactivations of two different owners never leave 0 active owners (exactly one succeeds)
owner_swap_note: Reactivation (active===true) takes NO lock and runs NO last-owner guard, so a legitimate swap (grant tenant-owner to B, then deactivate A while B is active) is unaffected: the guard sees B active → A not last → allowed. A concurrent reactivate-B + deactivate-A could at worst fail-CLOSED (spurious 409 on the deactivation if B isn't active yet) — never leaves 0 owners; the operator retries. Verified by the pre-existing 'with a SECOND owner present, deactivating one owner is allowed' test staying green.

anti_case: no case content in src (locking guard is generic owner/tenant substrate)
notes: Fix holds the owner-row lock only for the brief write-tx (KC calls remain OUTSIDE the tx, before it, per the existing KC-first flow) — no DB transaction is held across an external HTTP call. Compensation on the refused branch (re-enable KC) is best-effort with a console.warn fallback; if it fails the account stays PDP-active (DB authoritative) and the KC login is recoverable via a reactivate PATCH (ADR-T0727 §3.2). Broader coverage of OTHER last-owner-removal vectors (revoking the tenant-owner role_assignment directly rather than employee.deactivated_at) is out of T-0664 scope and would be the case for a DB-side trigger follow-up if ever needed.
